clue.text: Shrub first and last appearing on a field

blocks.note: A and Z are the first and last letters of the alphabet
taken as written
a lea is a meadow or grassy field, a poetic word

explanation.surface: A bush is the first and last thing to grow in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'appearing on' puts the alphabet's ends above A LEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The azalea is a flowering bush of the rhododendron family, grown widely in gardens.

clue.text: See compositor about layer to delete

blocks.note: comp is printers' short form for a compositor, who sets type
re means concerning, about
a hen is a layer of eggs
d is the proofreader's abbreviation for dele, the mark meaning remove this

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go and find the typesetter about a layer that must be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' reads as a stratum of text, but it is a bird that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To see a point is to understand or grasp it, the sense of comprehend.

clue.text: I sent tea around, being cordial

indicators.note: sending things around scatters them, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Handing round cups of tea makes the speaker seem friendly and warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like an adjective meaning friendly; here it is the noun, a sweet liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is an aniseed-flavoured liqueur, and a cordial is a sweet alcoholic drink of that kind.

clue.text: Band near the top in releases, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken word, so the answer only sounds like the word for releases

blocks.note: to release is to free, and frees sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: A musical band near the top of the charts is releasing records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests a pop group and 'releases' new records; in fact it is a decorative strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is a horizontal decorative strip running along a wall just below the ceiling or cornice.

clue.text: Word when going to get on prosperously

blocks.note: to fare is to get on or manage, as in 'how did you fare?'
doing well means prospering

explanation.surface: Someone says a word on leaving, hoping to do well in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Farewell is the parting expression said by someone leaving, a goodbye.

clue.text: Police body put down, cut up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: to inter is to bury, putting a body down in the ground
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A police corpse was buried and then chopped up, a grisly case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' suggests a corpse to go with 'put down' and 'cut up'; it means an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol is the international organisation coordinating police forces across many countries.

clue.text: Order sun when playing a game

indicators.note: playing about with something means moving it around, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A command to the sun, given while playing a game outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Rounders is a British bat-and-ball game played in schools, similar to baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounders is a team sport with a bat, ball and four bases, played mainly by British children.

clue.text: Northern drink raised spirit

indicators.note: something raised in a down entry is lifted upwards, so it is read bottom to top

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A northern beer gave the drinkers lifted spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' tempts with whisky after 'drink'; here it means verve.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is vigour, flair and dash, so it means spirit in the sense of liveliness.

clue.text: Check part of wineglass

blocks.note: first meaning: to halt or hold back a flow
second meaning: the slender column between bowl and foot

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a piece of a wine glass.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem bleeding is to stop it, and a glass's narrow shaft is its stem.

clue.text: Sound of collecting-tin upset?

blocks.note: first meaning: the clattering noise of coins shaken in a tin
second meaning: to unnerve or fluster someone

explanation.surface: Was it a knocked-over charity tin that made that noise?
explanation.definitionFit: Coins shaken in a tin make a clattering noise, and to unsettle someone is to fluster them.

clue.text: A station took in the traitor

blocks.note: taken as written
a post is a station, a place where someone is stationed on duty
to take food in is to eat it

explanation.surface: A railway station took the traitor in, giving refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took in' looks like a container signal but simply means consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons their faith or party, which makes them a renegade or deserter.

clue.text: With which one can get weaving!

definitions.text: With which one can get weaving!

blocks.note: surface reading: the idiom meaning get a move on, start working hard

blocks.clueFragment: With which one can get weaving!
blocks.note: setter's reading: the two sets of threads a loom needs to make cloth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get weaving' is British slang for hurry up; read literally it means weave cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The lengthwise and crosswise threads of a woven fabric are the basic materials of weaving.

clue.text: One up with pop?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone sitting up with their father
setter's reading: a jockey is 'up' riding a horse, and the records are pop music

explanation.walkthrough: A rider is said to be 'up' on a horse, so a record-spinning broadcaster rides pop records.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter who plays recorded popular music on radio or at clubs is known by this name.

clue.text: One nonetheless to live outside prison

indicators.note: being outside means wrapping round the other words, so the verb's letters enclose them

blocks.note: a means one
still means nevertheless
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Someone is determined to live outside jail despite everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the notorious Paris fortress jail stormed in 1789, so the word names a prison.

clue.text: Quick to contain injury in dispensary

indicators.note: one word is to contain another, holding it inside its own letters

blocks.note: pacy means fast
harm is damage or injury

explanation.surface: Hurry to stop the injury getting worse at the clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispensary is where medicines are made up and handed out, the job of a chemist's shop.

clue.text: One lesson is about an animal

indicators.note: about suggests being moved around, so the letters are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single school lesson is about an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioness is a female lion, a big cat and so an example of an animal.

clue.text: Waste a time with ace being prepared

indicators.note: something prepared is made up or worked over, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Throw away a moment while an ace serve is being readied in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to make thin and wasted, the verb sense of waste as in wasting away.

clue.text: The stuff presented to the viewer is nonsense

definitions.text: The stuff presented to the viewer

blocks.clueFragment: The stuff presented to the viewer
blocks.note: first meaning: lotion applied to the organ of sight, the viewer
second meaning: rubbish, claptrap

explanation.surface: A grumble that television offers its audience rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewer' suggests a TV watcher; it is the organ doing the viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion for bathing sore orbs shares its name with an informal word for humbug or claptrap.

clue.text: He has decisive qualities

blocks.note: surface reading: a man of firm, resolute character
setter's reading: a person whose role is deciding a contest, a judge

explanation.walkthrough: 'Decisive qualities' sounds like a personality trait; it means his job is to decide.
explanation.definitionFit: This person judges a competition and delivers the final ruling, so deciding is the role.

clue.text: Intelligence headquarters

blocks.note: surface reading: the head office of a spy agency
setter's reading: the bony quarters in the head where the brain lives

explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' suggests spying and 'headquarters' an office; literally they are the skulls housing brains.
explanation.definitionFit: Skulls enclose the brain, the seat of intelligence, so they are literally its quarters in the head.

clue.text: Distribute flesh, say ...

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word, so only its sound matters

blocks.note: flesh is meat, which sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: Hand out the meat, linking on to the next clue about food.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 21, making a butcher's scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to allot or dole out shares, especially of punishment.

clue.text: ...  and search for food

blocks.note: first meaning: to dig or rummage about
second meaning: informal word for things to eat

explanation.surface: Continuing from 20, someone hunts around for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To root about in soil is one sense, and slang for eats or nosh is the other.

clue.text: This is a bit phoney

blocks.note: surface reading: something slightly fake
setter's reading: a bit of a telephone, the part held to the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Phoney' means fake, but here it is 'of a phone': a component of a handset.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a telephone receiver you listen through is one component of the handset.

clue.text: Plant's trouble kept back

indicators.note: going back means reading the letters from right to left

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
had means kept or held

explanation.surface: A factory's problem was hushed up and held in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden flower with showy blooms grown from tubers, so it is a plant.

clue.text: One giving out around a billion to arouse hostility

indicators.note: being around something means enclosing it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: an emitter is something that sends out signals or radiation
b is the abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: Someone handing out a billion pounds stirs up resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: To embitter someone is to make them resentful, which provokes hostility and ill feeling.

clue.text: Snappy costume?

blocks.note: first meaning: irritable, bad-tempered, an old sense linked to liverish
second meaning: the uniform worn by servants or a company's colours

explanation.walkthrough: 'Snappy costume' looks like a smart outfit; snappy here means irritable, an adjective sense from a disordered liver.
explanation.definitionFit: A uniform worn by retainers is a livery, and an irritable, peevish person was once called livery.
